prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Weekly On-Call Rotation Schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Week 14(Mar 30 – Apr 5)" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Week 15(Apr 6 – 12)" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Week 16(Apr 13 – 19)" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Week" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 119px
  col 2: header "Role" · longest unbreakable word 78px · one-line width 78px
  col 3: header "Engineer" · longest unbreakable word 91px · one-line width 129px
  col 4: header "Phone" · longest unbreakable word 46px · one-line width 132px
  col 5: header "Escalation notes" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 655px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Show who is on call each week, how to reach them, and what to do when an issue needs escalation.","reading":"Readers find the current week, distinguish primary from secondary coverage, then follow the row to the engineer, phone number and escalation instructions. The week cells span both roles, so their height can absorb some wrapping.","groups":["Week and Role establish the coverage period and priority; each week groups a primary and secondary row.","Engineer and Phone identify and contact the person assigned to each role.","Escalation notes give the follow-up instructions associated with each assignment."],"keep_intact":["Phone numbers should remain recognizable and preferably on one line for reliable dialing.","Engineer names and role labels should remain whole where possible.","Week numbers and date ranges should remain easy to associate with their two rows."],"may_wrap":["Escalation notes can wrap at word boundaries.","Week labels and date ranges can occupy separate lines within the merged cells.","Engineer names can wrap between words if needed."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[65,70,83,74,67],"idea":"Fit the entire table in the viewport, accepting broken words and phone numbers in exchange for seeing every column at once."},{"name":"B","widths":[90,99,112,153,150],"idea":"Use moderate horizontal scrolling to keep roles and phone numbers intact while letting names, dates and notes wrap."},{"name":"C","widths":[140,99,150,153,220],"idea":"Favor legibility with wider columns that keep weeks, names and phone numbers on one line and give the notes more room, at the cost of substantial horizontal scrolling."}]}
